notes: 1 section header — too few for a contents list.
Heading levels skip: jumps h4 to h6. Needs a person.
488 words with no section headers at all — the biggest single improvement available here.

decisions.label: Turn the headings into section headers
decisions.why: 2 headings are plain text where every other page uses a section header, so the page reads as one continuous wall instead of parts.

decisions.label: Put the contact details in a paragraph
decisions.why: The names and numbers sit as loose text directly inside the contact block, which is what the old editor left and what nothing can space or style.

decisions.label: Tag a document link with the format it opens
decisions.why: 66 links on this page open a file — 66 PDF — and say nothing about it, while others in the same list carry a tag because their author typed one. The format is read from the file name, so the list stops being half-labelled. No link text changes.

decisions.label: Give the sub-headings their rule
decisions.why: 1 sub-heading is plain bold text. The design has a treatment for them — a teal rule down the left and a line across — and it had never been used on any page, because it needs a wrapper an author would have to know about.

decisions.label: Drop the dash once the link is set apart
decisions.why: 58 of those items separate the link from its description with a dash. The link is now set in the display face at a larger size with a chevron after it, so the dash marks a boundary that is already unmistakable. Only the separator is removed — no word changes.

decisions.label: Separate a link from its description
decisions.why: 58 list items open with a link and then explain it, all at the same weight — so the thing you can click is no easier to find than the sentence about it. The link becomes the item and the explanation sits under it.

decisions.label: Retire the old banner graphic
decisions.why: It repeats the page title in picture form, which the new banner already does in type.
